# Bidcraft — extended product context

Bidcraft is an AI-assisted tender and RFP proposal workspace. Its purpose is to help teams organise requirements, write evidence-backed responses, identify possible gaps, and maintain a useful revision history. Its tagline is “Make every bid count.”

## Workflow
1. Create a new tender with its title, contracting authority, and budget. New workspaces start without another tender’s clauses, proposal, history, or compliance claims.
2. Import requirements from pasted text, JPEG, PNG, WebP, or PDF documents of up to 5 MB. AI extraction may return multiple clauses. Review extracted text and responses.
3. Search the corporate evidence library. Live embeddings are used when available; otherwise deterministic local text similarity ranks documents. The interface identifies the mode.
4. Inspect tender requirements and responses in side-by-side or overlay views. Manually edit a response or request AI assistance. Manual edits need a fresh compliance review.
5. Run an AI compliance audit to record possible discrepancies and suggested wording. Applying a suggestion is not proof of compliance. Recheck the proposal and source evidence.
6. Save and compare immutable proposal snapshots. Restoring a version creates a new snapshot and preserves revision history.
7. Export the proposal as Markdown. The app does not submit bids to procurement portals.

## Bid Anatomy and human review
The Bid Anatomy tab shows an SVG inspection bench connected to the selected tender. Pins retract only for recorded human approvals; the gauge measures reviewed mandatory clauses. Larger tenders use six-station pages. Users can inspect original requirements, draft responses, open flags, and full linked evidence records. They can manage evidence links, open the matching comparison clause, approve a reviewed response, or request changes with a note.

Reviews are displayed in SAST and use an ISO timestamp and the label Local reviewer, not an authenticated identity. Missing responses, unavailable evidence, non-compliant responses, and unresolved flags prevent approval. Editing proposal text, replacing a draft with an AI result or fix, and changing evidence links invalidate the previous review. Human Review snapshots preserve the decision, and version restoration restores it. A recorded approval does not guarantee legal eligibility.

## Storage and availability
Tender content and snapshots are stored in localStorage in the current browser. There is no cloud database, user account system, cross-device sync, or collaborative editing in this release. Clearing browser data removes local work. Export important drafts.

A production service worker caches visited pages and static assets for offline use. Offline availability depends on a previous online visit. AI requests are not cached and require an internet connection and a server configured with GEMINI_API_KEY. Local editing, snapshots, exports, and local text similarity do not require that key.

## Evidence boundaries
The starter tenders and evidence library are fictional demonstration content. Do not claim their insurance limits, certifications, past contract awards, financial standing, or delivery commitments as the user’s capabilities. An AI-generated score is a review aid, not a legal opinion, certification, or guarantee of eligibility or award. Human reviewers must validate source documents, dates, requirements, and commitments.

## Design and accessibility
Bidcraft uses an ivory, ink, teal, and chartreuse palette, a folded-document B logo, keyboard-accessible workspace tabs, native modal dialogs, and short interface transitions. The decorative Three.js scene respects reduced-motion preferences and provides a static fallback when WebGL is unavailable.

## Public resources
- / : Product introduction and tender workspace.
- /about : Product workflow and guidance.
- /llms.txt : Concise information for AI readers.
- /llm.txt : Compatibility alias with the same content.
- /manifest.webmanifest : App install metadata.
- /robots.txt : Crawl rules; API paths are excluded.
- /sitemap.xml : Public page URLs when APP_URL is configured.

## South African tender discovery
- [Find South African tenders](/tenders): Search National Treasury's advertised tender notices by keyword, province, buyer, category, procurement type, closing window, publication window and briefing requirement. Filters have shareable URLs.
- Source records are public Treasury data, separate from the workspace's demonstration tenders. Coverage is incomplete and source endpoints can change. Freshness, unavailable values and timestamp conflicts are shown; original documents govern submission requirements.
- Users can save notices in this browser and create a blank bid workspace with source attribution, ZAR and SAST metadata. Re-import opens an existing bid rather than overwriting it.
- Saved notices and recent successful search pages are browser-local copies without cross-device sync or downloaded attachments. Failed source refreshes must not be described as fresh, successful searches.
- Tender discovery does not require a paid tender API or Gemini configuration. AI drafting, audits and OCR still require the server-side Gemini key.

## South African market defaults
- The primary market is South Africa. The interface uses South African English (en-ZA), rand (ZAR), and South African Standard Time (SAST, UTC+02:00). Source currencies and saved proposal content are preserved. VAT is not added automatically.
- Starter workspaces are clearly labelled fictional South African demonstrations. Existing drafts are not rewritten; older users can add the new examples without replacing their work.
- [South African bidding guide](/about#sa-bidding-guide) links to official CSD, SARS and the dtic guidance. CSD, tax status, B-BBEE evidence, preference goals, bid forms, CIDB and COIDA requirements depend on the actual bid documents. Bidcraft does not verify registrations or calculate preference points.
- AI features process supplied documents through the server and Gemini. Users must assess their POPIA obligations; the app makes no guarantee of POPIA compliance or South-African-only processing.
